Property & Entitlement Status

Developer's Dozen acquired the site in May 2022. Since then, the lot split and subdivision have cleared the City of San Diego and every environmental agency but one.

Base zoning
13
Entitled single-family lots, 5k–20k sq ft each
  • San Diego Development Services Division (DSD) has approved the lot split and subdivision.
  • CA Fish & Game, US Army Corps of Engineers, Regional Water Quality Control Board, and the Federal EPA have all provided concurrence.
  • US Fish & Wildlife wetlands mitigation plan is the one remaining item, currently in process (long-term mitigation plan).
  • Two of the thirteen homes will be designated at 130% of AMI as part of the affordability compliance path.
Track Record

Every Step, Documented

This isn't a speculative concept. The City of San Diego approved this exact 13-lot subdivision once before, and Developer's Dozen has spent five years since acquisition methodically closing out what remains — every milestone below is backed by an executed agreement, City submittal, or third-party report.

2001
City first approved this 13-lot concept on this site
14
Documented milestones, contract to present
Late-Stage
Independent Jan. 2026 entitlement status review
Original Entitlement · City of San Diego (Prior Ownership)
Apr 2001
Original 13-lot site plan approved
The City approves Exhibit "A" — the subdivision of the 3.11-acre site into 13 lots for single-family homes and the extension of Mount Albertine Avenue.
Nov 30, 2001
Planning Commission grants MMRP permit
The City of San Diego Planning Commission grants Permit No. 99-0125 — recorded City precedent for building exactly this project on this site.
Acquisition & Due Diligence
Jul 2021
Purchase agreement executed
All-cash agreement signed to acquire the site for $1,650,000, opening a due-diligence period ahead of closing.
Aug 30, 2021
Entitlement findings prepared
During due diligence, formal findings are drafted supporting the Neighborhood Development Permit and the specific code deviations the 13-lot layout requires under current zoning — work begins before the deal even closes.
May 5, 2022
Close of escrow
Title vests in Developer's Dozen. Due diligence complete; the sponsor now controls the entitlement process directly.
Active Entitlement Processing
Aug 1, 2022
City project transferred to new owner
The prior owner formally relinquishes involvement in City Project No. 603759; Developer's Dozen assumes active processing.
Sep 22, 2022
Formal resubmittal to the City
Project team responds to City plan-check comments across the Tentative Map, Site Development Permit, Planned Development Permit, and Easement Vacation applications.
Oct 26, 2022
Traffic & VMT study submitted
Transportation scoping and Vehicle Miles Traveled analysis submitted to the City for the 13-unit project.
Dec 2022 – Jan 2023
Community Planning Group review
Project presented to the Clairemont Mesa Community Planning Group. No adverse recommendation or opposition is recorded against the project.
Sep 21, 2023
City review cycle advances
Outstanding plan-check items narrowed with the City across environmental, land-use, and engineering disciplines.
2024 – 2025
Technical studies finalized
Geotechnical, drainage/SWQMP, infiltration, biology, and mobility/VMT reports completed; environmental review advances toward agency concurrence.
2025
Sponsor pushes City responsiveness
Deposit account kept active through continued plan-check; sponsor formally escalates with the City to keep processing on schedule.
Final Stretch
Jan 26, 2026
Independent status review: late-stage entitlement
Third-party review confirms the project is "substantially de-risked," with remaining approvals procedural rather than discretionary — estimated 6–9 months to final permit issuance.
Jun – Sep 2026
Wetland mitigation credits secured
Available credits identified at the Crestridge and Willow Road conservation banks; option agreement executed with the Otay River Mitigation Bank — closing out the one remaining outside-agency item, U.S. Fish & Wildlife wetlands mitigation.
Sourced, not summarized. Every date above traces to an executed agreement, City submittal, or third-party report in the project file, available to investors upon request.

Annualized ROI
Methodology: preferred return accrues simple-interest on your invested capital for the selected hold period. Remaining profit after that preferred return is split 50/50 (editable) between all LP investors and the sponsor; your share of the LP pool is pro-rata to your investment ÷ $3,000,000 total raise. Figures recompute live and may differ slightly from the illustrative example in the original deck, which used rounded assumptions.

Site & Renderings

The Neighborhood

Thirteen homesites on a quiet cul-de-sac off Mt. Albertine Avenue — a wooded infill setting surrounded by established San Diego neighborhoods, walkable to Mission Valley and minutes from Mission Bay.

The Residence

Mid-century architecture built for indoor/outdoor living — board-formed concrete, black steel glazing, and warm wood screening at dusk.

Interiors

Open-plan living and kitchen, double-height great room, and a primary suite designed around light and view.

Two Distinct Models

1 variation plus 2 reverse floorplans. Lot sizes range from 5,000 to 20,000 square feet.

Mid-Century Architecture

2,000–2,400 sq. ft., two stories, designed around indoor/outdoor living.

Ease of Build

Bold simplicity, flexible living, sunken living rooms — designed by Basile Studio and Jules Wilson Design Studio.
